summary: Console usage panels show duplicated token counts near hourly rollup boundaries (double-counting)
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that the Console's usage dashboard is showing token usage that appears to be approximately double the expected values for specific hourly windows. Impact: Billing and forecasting confusion for a paying enterprise customer; potential overbilling perception. Environment: prod / us-east (Console + Usage Aggregation service + Billing export). Observed since 2026-03-09 23:00 UTC after an internal rollout of an aggregation change.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to Console as a customer admin for Candela Health
2) Navigate to Console -> Usage -> Hourly breakdown for last 48 hours
3) Observe token counts around the hour boundary 2026-03-09 22:00-23:00 UTC and 23:00-00:00 UTC
4) Compare raw request logs (export) to Console rollup values; raw logs do NOT show duplicate requests but Console panel shows sums consistent with overlap
5) Query billing export S3 CSV for the same time window and compare to Console panel totals

2026-03-10 10:05 - Marco Chen (SRE): Noted that aggregation job was rolled out 2026-03-09 22:45 UTC. Collecting agg-worker logs and billing export. Marked ticket P1 and escalated to infra on-call.

investigation_notes: Agg-worker change: previous rollup algorithm used [start_ts, end_ts) semantics. A change in commit abcd123 inadvertently switched to inclusive end for a subset of workers, which led to overlapping assignment of requests that landed exactly at boundary timestamps.
Overlap manifested primarily for requests with millisecond timestamps that got normalized to second boundaries in the rollup layer.
Billing export pipeline uses raw-event ingestion and separate hourly grouping; it did not double-count. Console was reading from the aggregated datastore which reflected the overlap.

Scope: affected rollups for a 6-hour window around the deployment; approx 0.9% of total hourly tokens for affected hours were double-counted but appeared as ~100% duplication for narrow windows with low volume.
Mitigation path considered: 1) Recompute rollups (chosen), 2) Rollback aggregate change (not desirable due to other fixes), 3) Display temporary warning in Console (short-term fallback).
root_cause: A code change deployed to the usage aggregation service changed rollup window semantics to include the end timestamp for some worker instances. This caused the same event timestamps that normalize to the boundary second to be counted in both adjacent hourly buckets.
resolution: Fixed the rollup window calculation so it consistently uses start-inclusive, end-exclusive semantics across all workers (hotfix PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4721)
Ran a targeted backfill job to recompute hourly rollups for impacted hours (jobs completed successfully and verified)
Validated Console totals against billing-export CSV and raw logs, then notified customer and finance with corrected numbers
resolution_deployment: Hotfix deployed to agg-worker pool on 2026-03-12T01:10Z. Backfill finished 2026-03-12T03:45Z.
next_steps: Ship additional unit and integration tests to assert rollup window semantics (to prevent regressions)
Add monitoring alert for sudden hour-over-hour doubling deltas in aggregated datastore versus raw-event export
Run a one-time reconciliation job to compare aggregate vs raw export weekly for the next month
